summary: In-place formatter that overwrites the first non-digit character of a numeric string with the locale decimal separator byte_5E6BD8 and left-shifts the remaining tail by one byte, returning the character displaced out the end (normally the string terminator). Character classification is single-byte (off_5E69C8 lookup) or multi-byte (CharacterEncodingConvertViaLookupTableFallback) depending on cbMultiByte.

local_names.v1: working scan pointer advanced to the first non-digit character
local_names.v2: digit-class flag from the char-type table
local_names.result: character carried forward through the left-shift, returned at the end
local_names.v4: write pointer one past v1, driven through the shift loop
local_names.v5: character read from *v4 during the shift

operations.description: Set v1 = a1 so the scan starts at the first byte of the string.
If sub_58B465(*a1) already returns 101 the first character is digit-class and no scan runs; otherwise scan forward from v1.

Advance v1 while the current character classifies as digit-class: when cbMultiByte <= 1 read the flag v2 = off_5E69C8[0][*v1] & 4 from the char-type table, otherwise use the multi-byte classifier CharacterEncodingConvertViaLookupTableFallback(*v1, 4).
Save result = *v1 (the first non-digit character, or the terminator) and overwrite the character at v1 with the decimal separator byte_5E6BD8.

Left-shift the string tail starting at v4 = v1 + 1 (the second byte when v1 is the string head at this:0x0): repeatedly store result into *v4, read *v4 as the new result, and advance v4 while the byte just read is non-zero.
Return the final displaced character (the string terminator carried out of the end of the shift).

clean_pseudocode: do { char v5 = *v4; *v4 = result; result = v5; } while (*v4++);
